title: Support Ops Task-Graph Refinery: convert runbooks into safe, schedulable task graphs
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Support engineers still run many manual runbook steps during incidents. Runbooks exist in Confluence and ad-hoc scripts in the admin repo. This leads to variability, longer MTTR, and unreviewed privileged operations.

Goal: Build a 'Refinery' service that consumes an annotated runbook, synthesizes a deterministic task-graph (ops-graph), applies safety gates and parameter validation, and emits an executable task bundle that the Admin CLI / Ops Console can schedule or replay. The task-graph should preserve human-readable step metadata for audits and support dry-run simulation.

Scope:
- Parser for annotated Markdown/Confluence-styled runbooks (action primitives and intents)
- Heuristic conversion to a directed acyclic task graph (with explicit compensating and rollback nodes)
- Safety gate layer (RBAC checks, token scoping, approval steps for high-priv ops)
- Dry-run simulator that runs in sandbox with mocked resources
- Integration hooks: Admin CLI (opsctl), Console task-runner UI, and runbook storage index

Out-of-scope for this ticket: execution backends (we'll call the existing ops-runner), long-term archival UI polishing, and enterprise SSO integration (handled in separate EPIC).

Success criteria (acceptance):
- End-to-end conversion of three canonical runbooks into task-graphs (db-rollout, model-cache-warm, emergency-scale-down) with deterministic outputs and no manual edits.
- Safety gates block any task that would run destructive operations without explicit approval in test harness.
- Telemetry emitted to Grafana showing task-graph creation times, validation failures, and dry-run success rate.
- PRs merged for parser + simulator and a demo in the ops lab showing 2x faster median incident completion in synthetic tests.

Telemetry & dashboards:
- https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/ops-refinery/refinery-metrics
- Counters: refinery.jobs.created, refinery.validation.failures, refinery.dryrun.success, refinery.execution.attempts

Links & artifacts:
- Design brief: https://confluence.redwood.internal/display/OPS/Task-Graph+Refinery+Design
- Reference runbooks: https://confluence.redwood.internal/display/OPS/Runbook+Library
- Prototype repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops-refinery (WIP branch: dev/synth)

Approval UX friction: if safety gates are too strict we increase MTTR
Scope creep into execution backend changes or enterprise SSO requirements
